messages.text: Claro! Podemos criar uma app. Me conta a ideia: o que ela deve fazer e quem vai usar?

GROOM — Barber Booking Platform
PROJECT OVERVIEW

Create a premium, modern and fully responsive SaaS web application dedicated to barbershops and professional barbers.

The platform should allow customers to discover barbershops, book appointments online and manage their bookings.

It should also provide barbershop owners and barbers with a complete management dashboard to control appointments, customers, services, staff, schedules and business performance.

The product takes inspiration from the functionality and simplicity of Setmore, but MUST have its own original brand identity, visual language, interface and user experience.

Do not copy Setmore's layouts, branding, colors or components.

The working brand name is GROOM.

1. BRAND IDENTITY AND DESIGN

Create a premium, minimalist and sophisticated visual identity.

Brand personality:

Modern
Premium
Confident
Masculine without being stereotypical
Minimalist
Professional
Technology-driven

Color palette:

Primary background: #111111
Secondary background: #1B1B1B
Accent: #C5A46D
Main text: #F5F0E8
Secondary text: #999999
Borders: #303030

Typography:

Use a sophisticated modern sans-serif font.
Large editorial-style headings.
Clean and readable interface typography.

Design guidelines:

Premium dark interface.
Elegant spacing and alignment.
Subtle transitions and animations.
Rounded corners used sparingly.
Beautiful calendar and dashboard components.
High-quality barber photography.
Responsive layouts for desktop, tablet and mobile.

Avoid generic templates, excessive gradients, cartoon illustrations and unnecessary decorative elements.

The result should look like a serious premium SaaS startup.

2. USER ROLES

Create three user roles:

Customer
Barbershop Owner / Administrator
Barber / Staff Member

Each role must have its own permissions and personalized dashboard.

3. PUBLIC WEBSITE

Create a modern landing page containing:

Premium hero section.
Clear headline and call to action.
Search bar to find barbershops.
Featured barbershops.
Popular services.
How the platform works.
Benefits for barbershop owners.
Pricing section.
FAQ section.
Professional footer.

Main CTA buttons:

Find a Barbershop
Book an Appointment
Register Your Barbershop
4. CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE

Customers must be able to:

Register and log in.
Browse available barbershops.
View individual barbershop profiles.
See services, prices and durations.
View barber profiles and photos.
Select a service.
Select a barber.
Choose an available date and time.
Confirm appointments.
View upcoming appointments.
Reschedule or cancel appointments according to business policies.
View appointment history.
Manage personal information.

The booking experience must be extremely simple and intuitive.

5. BARBERSHOP MANAGEMENT DASHBOARD

Create a professional dashboard with a sidebar navigation.

Dashboard sections:

Overview
Calendar
Appointments
Customers
Services
Team Members
Working Hours
Business Profile
Settings

Overview dashboard:

Today's appointments.
Upcoming appointments.
Total customers.
Monthly revenue.
Completed appointments.
Cancellation statistics.

Use attractive charts and clear data visualizations.

6. APPOINTMENT CALENDAR

Create a fully functional appointment management system.

Calendar views:

Day
Week
Month

Features:

Display appointments by barber.
Different colors for appointment statuses.
Create appointments manually.
Edit appointments.
Cancel appointments.
Block unavailable time slots.
Configure breaks and holidays.
Prevent double bookings.
Automatically calculate available appointment slots based on service duration and barber availability.

Appointment statuses:

Pending
Confirmed
Completed
Cancelled
No-show
7. SERVICES MANAGEMENT

Allow administrators to:

Create services.
Edit services.
Delete services.
Set service names.
Add descriptions.
Upload service images.
Set prices.
Set appointment durations.
Assign services to specific barbers.

Example services:

Haircut
Skin Fade
Beard Trim
Haircut + Beard
Hair Wash
Premium Grooming
8. TEAM MANAGEMENT

Allow barbershop owners to:

Add team members.
Edit barber profiles.
Upload profile pictures.
Set individual working hours.
Assign services.
Configure days off.
View individual calendars.
Manage team permissions.

Each barber must have an individual schedule.

9. CUSTOMER MANAGEMENT

Create a customer database containing:

Customer name.
Email.
Phone number.
Appointment history.
Total appointments.
Last visit.
Internal notes.

Allow administrators to search and filter customers.

10. PUBLIC BARBERSHOP BOOKING PAGE

Every registered barbershop must have its own unique public booking page.

Example URL structure:

/barbershop/barbershop-name

Each page must include:

Business logo.
Cover image.
Business description.
Location.
Contact information.
Opening hours.
Services and prices.
Barber profiles.
Available appointment slots.
Booking functionality.

The page should reflect the barbershop's identity while maintaining the platform's premium design standards.

11. DATABASE AND BACKEND

Use Supabase for:

Authentication.
PostgreSQL database.
User profiles.
Barbershop records.
Services.
Staff members.
Appointments.
Customer records.
Storage for profile and business images.

Implement proper database relationships and Row Level Security (RLS).

Users must only access data they are authorized to see.

Customers must not access private business management information.

Barbers must only access the information permitted by their role.

Business owners must manage their own barbershops and associated data.

12. BOOKING LOGIC

This is one of the most important parts of the application.

Implement real appointment availability.

The system must:

Check barber working hours.
Check service duration.
Account for breaks and days off.
Check existing appointments.
Prevent overlapping appointments.
Update availability immediately after a confirmed booking.
Prevent two customers from booking the same time slot.

All appointment times must be stored consistently and displayed in the barbershop's local timezone.

13. NOTIFICATIONS

Prepare the architecture for:

Booking confirmation emails.
Appointment reminder emails.
Cancellation notifications.
Rescheduling notifications.

Do not simulate successful email delivery if no email service is configured.

14. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Build a real functional application, not just a static prototype.
Use reusable components.
Use clean and maintainable code.
Ensure responsive design.
Include loading states.
Include empty states.
Include error handling.
Include form validation.
Protect private routes.
Implement role-based permissions.
Use Supabase as the backend.
15. DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES

Build the application in a structured way.

Priority 1:

Brand identity.
Landing page.
Authentication.
Customer dashboard.
Barbershop dashboard.

Priority 2:

Services management.
Staff management.
Appointment calendar.
Booking system.

Priority 3:

Notifications.
Analytics.
Payments.
Advanced integrations.

IMPORTANT:

Focus on building a beautiful, coherent and functional MVP first.

Do not create buttons that do nothing.

Do not use fake data as if it were real production data.

Use realistic demonstration data only where appropriate and clearly distinguish it from real user data.

The final product should feel like a premium, polished SaaS platform built specifically for the barber industry.

Não alterei arquivos. O código fornecido está ligado a um modelo de restaurantes, mesas e reservas; o pedido exige serviços, barbeiros e horários individuais, além de regras de acesso e disponibilidade que ainda não existem nesse modelo. Trocar apenas a marca e a interface apresentaria como funcionais recursos que o backend atual não suporta. Para fazer a conversão de forma funcional, é necessário incluir as alterações de banco de dados, RLS e lógica de agendamento no escopo de publicação.

Nenhuma alteração foi publicada no GitHub.
